componentAcceptance: All T04 criteria are covered. Two same-model non-Main Bots keep separate Sessions, principals and exact model grants. One Bot's saved memory is visible after its workspace-driven Session rotation, while the other Bot's recall returns no entry. The real product test initially exposed cross-workspace file reads; a new composition guard now resolves real paths and confines read/read_image/glob/grep to the current Session workspace, including junction/symlink escape refusal. A real pwsh attempt returns BOT_NATIVE_EXECUTION_DENIED, so native shell cannot bypass the read guard. Existing cross-Bot Task/machine/receipt denial and per-operation CLI h-<operationId> profile evidence remains.
productAcceptance: T04 passes at integration level. Private chats, memory, rotated Sessions, restricted directories and per-attempt CLI profiles do not leak between same-model Bots; explicitly delegated input remains the intended shared content. Formal scores are 0/20 work packages, 23/63 scenarios and M0 11/12.
implementation: Added a composition-layer real-path read guard and native pwsh execution denial for Bot Sessions; frozen DS and SDK sources were not changed.
The guard is disposed with the composed product, fails closed without trusted folder identity and is included in the npm published file list.
The default product probe now exercises memory, private file, Session rotation, cross-directory read and native shell paths, followed by cold-start checks.
testRuns: npm run integration:probe-product-default: all 44 checks pass, including two new T04 checks and all existing Task, credential and restart checks.
Workspace privacy + lifecycle + product composition: 25/25; CLI contract/renewal + authority/policy: 26/26.
Final npm test: phase one 1593/1589/0/4 and phase two 387/303/0/84; total 1980 tests, 1892 pass, 0 fail, 88 skipped. npm run check:client: OK.
preservedFailures: Before the guard, the real cross-Bot read returned the other Bot's private file successfully. This was a genuine product isolation defect and is now fixed.
The first root regression found the new module absent from package.json files. It is now explicitly published and the complete root passes.

Schema restriction alone did not remove built-in pwsh from the model-facing list. The final control enforces BOT_NATIVE_EXECUTION_DENIED at execution and tests a real rejected call instead of relying on tool visibility.
Fixture corrections distinguished Bot IDs from rotated Session IDs and treated a no-memory response containing the query text as no entry, not a memory leak.
limitations: This is a product tool/session boundary, not separate OS-account isolation; T25 remains the OS isolation gate.
The CLI model and memory workflows use deterministic offline fixtures. No real model inference, real credential, production profile, push or release was used.
